findings.headline: Beyond whether it works, engineers' two biggest objections are that AI deskills or replaces them ({count:deskills_or_replaces_engineers} of {n_base} posts) and that it needs access to production ({count:data_access_and_security}). None of the {vendors_rated} options mapped here shows proof on either.
findings.short: Beyond “does it work?”, engineers' biggest objections are deskilling ({count:deskills_or_replaces_engineers} posts) and production access ({count:data_access_and_security}). None of the {vendors_rated} options mapped shows proof on either.
findings.implication: Investigations already shows proof that it works. On these two, its pages assert, as every option here does: you work the problem with the agent, and its only change is a pull request you review. Proof could be a responder explaining a cause afterwards, and a page showing how “pull request only” is enforced. The deskilling posts span {threads:deskills_or_replaces_engineers} threads.
findings.note: Post-launch review (20 Oct): three simulated reviewers (marketing lead, hiring, engineer) found the proof gap newer to the team than the DIY point; the old 'second most common since 2025' ranked counts three apart on noisy labels and printed the wrong n. verify.ts asserts the ranking and the zero-proof claim.

findings.headline: {diy:uses} of {n_base} posts use or recommend a general AI tool for incident work, {diy:uses:positive} of them positively, but only {diy:unneeded} argue that makes a dedicated product unnecessary.
findings.implication: Most aren't arguing against buying; they're using what they already have. incident.io already argues that in-house builds rarely measure accuracy, and ships a plugin for the agents engineers use. What's missing is a public side-by-side: Investigations and a bare model on the same past incidents, from the backtests it already runs daily.
findings.note: Post-launch review (20 Oct): the old headline set 73 (Sonnet's DIY tag) against 12 (Haiku's objection label); 13 'says a product is unnecessary' comes from the same tagger as 73. Hero line moved to f2 (was approved by Dany for this finding; flagged to him).

findings.headline: {either:wrong_or_hallucinated_cause+cant_verify_reasoning} of {n_base} posts say the AI gets the cause wrong or that its reasoning can't be checked.
findings.implication: Investigations answers both with proof: a measured jump in accurate early updates, and every hypothesis linked to its sources. The next question is how often it's wrong. Each customer sees that on its own homepage, and incident.io's buyer's guide tells evaluators to push for precision and recall. No option here publishes a figure yet; one from its backtests would meet that bar first.
findings.note: Post-launch review (20 Oct): 'publish misses' ignored that customers already see wins and misses on their homepage; 'sceptical' clause was a near-tautology. The precision-and-recall bar comes from incident.io's own buyer's guide.
